title: Vendor intake + privileged access & SLA alignment - Archimedes Health
summary: Initial procurement/gov intake to cover MSA exceptions, DPA clauses, SLA/entitlement needs for a pilot. Security team requested deeper KMS/VPC detail and a SOC2 artifact. Procurement clarified billing and PO path; legal flagged two DPA redlines. Agreed to a security deep-dive and to exchange marked-up MSA + pricing worksheet.
next_steps: Redwood: send marked MSA with highlighted exceptions by 2026-03-23
Redwood: upload SOC2 type 2 + KMS docs to shared drive by 2026-03-20
Archimedes: return vendor intake form and PO cadence details by 2026-03-24
Schedule security deep-dive (Priya + Ben + Ravi) for week of 2026-03-30
action_items: Maya Patel; Send redlined MSA and one-page exceptions summary; 2026-03-23
Ben Torres; Prepare brief KMS/VPC architecture note and checklist; 2026-03-20
Priya Singh; Provide vendor intake form and list of required audit fields; 2026-03-24
Mark Rivera; Confirm billing route (PO vs credit card) and procurement SLA approval path; 2026-03-24
header:
Date: Mon Mar 16 2026 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ben Torres (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Archimedes CTO), Mark Rivera (Archimedes Procurement), Sarah Lewis (Archimedes Legal), Priya Singh (Archimedes InfoSec), Evan Holt (Archimedes Platform)
Meeting type: Procurement / vendor onboarding - exceptions and security alignment
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, quick intros then we'll jump into the intake items, I'm Maya, AE on the account.
[00:08] Olivia Chen: Hi Maya, Olivia here, CTO at Archimedes. We're trying to finalize vendor gating for the generative features pilot.
[00:15] Mark Rivera: Mark from procurement, I'll lead the PO/billing path part.
[00:19] Sarah Lewis: Sarah legal - we'll focus on DPA/msa redlines.
[00:24] Priya Singh: Priya, InfoSec - we'll need SOC2 and specifics on key management.
[00:29] Ben Torres: Ben, SE - I'll cover architecture and how Redwood handles VPC/private deployments and KMS.
[00:34] Maya Patel: Great, high level agenda: MSA exceptions, DPA points, SLA and entitlements, security artifacts, and billing. We'll identify blockers for a pilot.
[00:42] [00:45] Ben Torres: Quick note - Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC. For regulated PHI-ish workloads you typically look at Private or Dedicated with encryption at rest and customer-managed KMS.
[00:58] Priya Singh: When you say customer-managed KMS, is that HSM-backed? We need key isolation and BYOK.
[01:06] Ben Torres: Yes, BYOK with support for customer Cloud KMS (we've done AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and HSM-backed keys via partner integrations in our Private offering. For the hosted path we offer envelope encryption but keys are Redwood-managed unless you go Private.
[01:22] Priya Singh: Ok that's helpful but we need to see the integration diagram and proof of separation.
[01:27] Ben Torres: We'll attach an architecture note, I'll put diagrams in the shared folder.
[01:31] Olivia Chen: On data residency — our pilot will run in us-east and we require data not leave region for logs and metric retention. Does Redwood support region pinning?
[01:41] Maya Patel: Yes, customers can pin region and we can configure retention for logs. For hosted we can route to regionally proxied endpoints. For Private it's straightforward since control plane sits in your VPC.
[01:50] Sarah Lewis: Turning to the DPA: we have two redlines — one around subprocessor disclosure cadence and another on deletion / return semantics for derivative models. We'd like a guaranteed timeline for subprocessor notices.
[02:05] Maya Patel: Understandable. Our standard is 30 days notice for new subprocessors; for Enterprise customers we can add contractual notice commitments and a listing mechanism.
[02:13] Sarah Lewis: We'd also like an explicit clause about suppression of training on customer data — we can't have customer data used to retrain public models.
[02:22] Ben Torres: For Dedicated and Private, there's no training on customer data. For Hosted we have opt-out language but we'll provide precise wording.
[02:29] Priya Singh: And audit logs — we need immutable audit logs for privileged access with 12 months retention. Is that possible?
[02:36] Ravi Kapoor: We can enable audit log retention to 12 months on Dedicated and Private, and streaming to your SIEM via secure forwarder. Immutable storage depending on your retention target is supported via S3 + Object Lock patterns.
[02:48] Priya Singh: Great, include that in the security note.
[02:51] [03:00] Mark Rivera: On billing — Archimedes prefers PO monthly invoices. Do you accept prepaid annual commitments or only monthly usage billing?
[03:08] Maya Patel: We support both. For pilots most customers do a monthly PO; Dedicated commitments are typically annual or monthly reserved. We'll share a pricing worksheet with the PO billing path options.
[03:18] Mark Rivera: Also need to know the path for approval. Our legal team needs MSA + DPA redlines before procurement signs.
[03:25] Sarah Lewis: Correct. We'll review redlines, then procurement will confirm. We may need an exec signoff depending on exceptions.
[03:31] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll send a redlined MSA that flags the two DPA clauses and a one-pager explaining Redwood's positions.
[03:38] Olivia Chen: For SLA: we are targeting 99.9% uptime for the pilot and latency SLOs sub 200ms p95 for short completions. What SLAs and remedies do you offer?
[03:49] Ben Torres: Our enterprise SLA varies by deployment. Hosted customers get a baseline SLA, Dedicated has stronger SLAs we can contractually bind, and Private is negotiated. Remedies range from service credits; for Dedicated we can provide tighter latency guarantees under capacity reservations.
[04:04] Olivia Chen: We might need a performance guardrail to ensure the pilot meets product metrics. Can we put a performance acceptance test in the SOW?
[04:12] Maya Patel: Yes, we typically include an acceptance criteria section tied to a benchmark harness — Redwood can run a sample workload with your prompts to validate p95 and throughput.
[04:21] Evan Holt: On entitlements, we'll need role-based access for product users and elevated access for platform engineers. How granular is RBAC?
[04:29] Ravi Kapoor: RBAC is per-route and per-environment; you can scope token permissions, feature flags and admin actions. We can create separate roles for product, infra, and auditing-only.
[04:39] Priya Singh: Does admin access include ability to view the KV cache or prompts? We need to separate PII visibility.
[04:46] Ben Torres: Admins can view request metadata but we support masking/obfuscation of prompt content for certain roles and field-level redaction before log storage. We'll include details in the security doc.
[04:58] [05:15] Sarah Lewis: On indemnity and liability caps in the MSA, our standard counsel seeks 6 months of direct damages cap for pilot vendors. Do you have flexibility?
[05:25] Maya Patel: We can discuss; standard Redwood caps are typically annual fees or a multiple, but enterprise exceptions are considered case-by-case. I'll flag to contracts team.
[05:34] Sarah Lewis: Also want to confirm deletion semantics: upon expiration or termination, we need a certification that all customer data has been destroyed and confirmation that derivative models are handled per the DPA clause.
[05:46] Ben Torres: We'll provide a data disposition certificate and a description of our model handling; for Dedicated/Private there is no training on customer data and artifacts can be purged on termination.
[05:56] Mark Rivera: Timeline question — procurement needs an expected contract turnaround to plan budget. What is typical for similar customers?
[06:04] Maya Patel: For standard MSA + DPA with minor redlines it's often 2-4 weeks. If there are enterprise exceptions it can extend to 6-8 weeks depending on security review time.
[06:13] Olivia Chen: We'd like to aim for a pilot start in early May. Is that realistic if we sign in late April?
[06:20] Maya Patel: Yes, that's feasible — we'll coordinate onboarding, a pilot checklist, and an enablement runbook.
[06:27] [06:45] Priya Singh: One more thing - can we get a list of subprocessors and an example subprocessor notice?
[06:33] Ben Torres: We'll include the current subprocessor list and an example notice template.
[06:38] Sarah Lewis: We'll also send our standard DPA redline tracker so you can indicate accept/decline per clause.
[06:45] Maya Patel: Great, action-wise Redwood will send: redlined MSA, SOC2 artifact, KMS and VPC architecture note, pricing worksheet. Customer to return intake form, PO cadence, and DPA redline tracker.
[06:58] [07:15] Ben Torres: Technical note for the security deep-dive — we'll include how KV cache is handled in Dedicated, eviction policies, and whether the cache persists on restarts.
[07:26] Priya Singh: That's crucial. If the cache holds any prompt data we need options to disable or encrypt the cache with customer keys.
[07:34] Ravi Kapoor: Cache encryption at rest with CMEK is supported; we'll document options to disable persistent caching for the pilot.
[07:44] Evan Holt: Are there known latency tradeoffs for disabling prefix caches? We need to understand cost implications vs performance.
[07:51] Ben Torres: Disabling cache will increase token costs and latency slightly; we'll include quant estimates in the pricing worksheet.
[07:59] [08:30] Mark Rivera: Procurement question — if we sign a pilot PO now and then expand, is there a smooth path to convert to reserved Dedicated capacity?
[08:39] Maya Patel: Yes, we can include an upgrade path in the SOW. Reserved Dedicated capacity has a conversion credit model to apply pilot spend toward a committed monthly/annual reservation.
[08:50] Sarah Lewis: Any case studies with regulated healthcare customers? We want references and a brief security contact.
[08:58] Maya Patel: We'll share anonymized case studies and a security contact.
[09:03] Olivia Chen: Ok let's recap next steps.
[09:06] Maya Patel: Recap: Redwood to send redlined MSA by 3/23, SOC2 + KMS doc by 3/20, pricing worksheet and upgrade path. Archimedes to return intake form, DPA redline tracker, and confirm PO cadence by 3/24. Schedule security deep-dive week of 3/30.
[09:28] Sarah Lewis: Sounds good.
[09:30] Mark Rivera: I'll follow up with procurement timeline.
[09:33] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the shared folder.
[09:37] Olivia Chen: Thanks all.
[09:40] [END] Note: minor transcription artifacts present (names/acronyms occasionally mis-typed by auto transcript).
